chapter: Early bands around Bay St. Louis
title: Joining August Sosia's band and its personnel
summary: After Maurice, Harry played in August Sosia's band; he lists its sax, trombone, trumpet, clarinet, drums, piano and bass players, and Chick (Eddie Palud).

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: What about, uh, after Maurice, who did you play with after that band?
That's the social band I played, August Social. After Maurice.
After Maurice. And how old were you when you went with Maurice? Five hours.
I think the four hours, that was in 20... 26, 25. Must have been earlier. About 25. And you were quite a youngster then. Oh yeah. I was a youngster because I wasn't married then.
And, uh, so you went with the Social Band, and that's when they had men in there. That's right. And who were the other men? Did we get them?
No, we didn't get Social's band. Nah, got to think again now. Well, you know, Edgar's one. Edgar, Social, August Social.
And the instruments too.
Edgar, Social, Saxophone. Mm-hmm. August, Social, Trombone. Uh, Franklin, William Franklin, Trumpet. Harry Fagnatou, Banjo. Norbert Maurice, Drum. Mm-hmm.
And, we can get it off from... The Social Band, you told us the drum of the saxophone, the trombone, the banjo.
And, uh, Thomas Fagnatou clarinet. That's my uncle, Thomas. Yeah? You know, the one that called Trinatou.
Yeah, he was clarinet. Yeah, clarinet.
There was no one. Uncle Trinatou, so. And, who else? We had one more. I can't include...
Edgar. Edgar. Oh, and his daughter.
Great True playing... Great True Social playing the piano. And, Giger playing the bass. That's right. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Uh...
And where did that band play?

We split up the jazz between that band and the other band. I had got out of the other band at that time. Uh-huh. And, the jazz was just split up from here, just like I told you, from here to Biloxon, from Bay St. Louis to Pilotson. Out that way the jazz was split up. Well, Chick wasn't playing music then. Yeah. Chick was playing before me. Yeah. Yeah, Chick was playing with old Geese. That's when I got, uh, out of Paul's band and played with old Geese. What was Chick playing?
Band-Dude. What's his name anyway? Eddie Palud.
Eddie Palud. And they call him Chick.
Chip. That's his brother-in-law. Brother-in-law.
Mm-hmm. How do you spell Palud, didn't you? P-A-L-L-O-A-D-E. Good, I'm glad we got it.
I can't get all those names, you know. We got it on the tape.
